text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Finance Minister Dimitar Kostov said Bulgaria might be able to introduce a currency board system by the end of February if the technical preparation is completed by then.
-- The executive bureau of the ruling Bulgarian Socialist Party (BSP) decided to nominate the outgoing Interior Minister Nikolai Dobrev for a prime minister, BSP press office said.
-- City and intercity bus fares in Bulgaria will rise by some 25 percent from Monday as a result of increased fuel prices, a senior Transport ministry official said.

-- Nikolai Dobrev is not competent in economics and his nomination for prime minister shows that the ruling Socialist party is keen on supressing street protests rather than concentrating on solving the economic crisis, Bulgaria's main opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) leader Ivan Kostov said.
-- UDF said it would step up street protests against the ruling Socialists if the parliament rejects the "salvation declaration" proposed by the UDF.
-- Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency supervisory board elected Yosif Iliev as board chairman .
-- Bulgaria will meet payments on its foreign debt in January through the State Fund for Reconstruction and Development, Finance Minister Dimitar Kostov said.

-- Bulgaria's main opposition Union of Democratic Forces (UDF) said the Military Prosecutor's Office had confirmed UDF allegations that Interior Ministry officials had illegally tapped telephones of UDF leaders.
